title: Fix indirect permission letters: `ri` is indirect read plus insert
summary: A security best practice article now correctly explains that permission letters r, i, m, d each represent one permission (read, insert, modify, delete), and corrects its examples to avoid over-granting indirect permissions.
key_points: Permission tokens consist of individual letters: r (read), i (insert), m (modify), d (delete), with lowercase meaning indirect
The read-only 'Report Runner' example now correctly uses 'r' instead of 'ri', which would have also granted indirect insert
Best practice guidance and keywords updated to reflect the correct interpretation of permission letters
Added references to official Microsoft Learn documentation on permissions
quote: so `ri` is indirect read **plus indirect insert**, `ii` repeats insert, and `mi` and `di` each add indirect insert
